The main U.S. program that pays for foreign governments' purchases of American weapons, services, and training. Section 23 of the Arms Export Control Act authorizes the President to finance partners' procurement; the annual appropriations act provides the money, mostly as grants, and partners usually spend it through [Foreign Military Sales](fms.qmd).

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 82 Stat. 1324](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/82/1324){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 2763](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2763?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 23(a): authority to finance procurement of defense articles, defense services, and design and construction services by friendly countries and international organizations.
- Sec. 23(a): limited authority to finance commercial leases of defense articles for Israel and Egypt.
- Sec. 23(b)-(c): for loans, repayment within 12 years unless a statute allows longer, and interest rules.
- Annual appropriations add conditions, including notice to the Appropriations Committees before committing funds for major defense equipment beyond what was justified.
- Recipients remain subject to [Leahy Laws](leahy-laws.qmd) vetting and the [coup restriction](sec7008-coup.qmd).

## Why it matters

FMF is the largest U.S. security assistance grant program, and a few partners, above all Israel and Egypt, have historically received most of it. Because it is State Department money spent on Defense Department sales, it sits at the center of the Title 22 security assistance system, in contrast to the Defense Department's own [Title 10 security cooperation](seccoop-2016.qmd) authorities. Country allocations, earmarks, and conditions in the appropriations act are where Congress shapes it.

## Current status

In force. Funded each year in Title IV of the State-foreign operations appropriations act. Check current status.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}

## Funding and administration

- **Account.** Foreign Military Financing Program, Title IV (International Security Assistance) in the [State-foreign ops appropriations](sfops-approps-annual.qmd).
- **Run by.** The State Department, which sets policy and country allocations, and the Defense Security Cooperation Agency, which administers the funds and the purchases.
- **Committees.** Authorizing, House Foreign Affairs and Senate Foreign Relations; appropriations, the House and Senate subcommittees for State and foreign operations.
